The error log indicates that the `test_device_init_level` test is failing. This test checks if devices are initialized in the correct order based on their specified initialization levels.

The test expects the initialization sequence to be `PRE_KERNEL_1`, `PRE_KERNEL_2`, then `POST_KERNEL`. The test drivers are designed to record a sequence number corresponding to their expected initialization order.

In `tests/kernel/device/src/test_driver_init.c`, the test drivers `my_driver_level_1` and `my_driver_level_2` have their initialization levels swapped in their `DEVICE_DEFINE` macros. `my_driver_level_1` is incorrectly set to `PRE_KERNEL_2`, and `my_driver_level_2` is incorrectly set to `PRE_KERNEL_1`. This causes them to initialize out of the expected order, leading to the test failure.

The fix is to swap the initialization levels for these two device definitions to match the intended sequence.

DEVICE_DEFINE(my_driver_level_2, MY_DRIVER_LV_2, &my_driver_lv_2_init,
